modes.label: H100 GPU cluster, on-demand (8-GPU nodes, per GPU-hour)
modes.note: H100 (80 GB) on-demand "$3.99/hr per GPU", scale "8 to 256 GPUs", self-serve, "pay hourly, terminate anytime" (https://www.together.ai/gpu-clusters and https://www.together.ai/pricing, 2026-09-28). Sold as whole bare-metal HGX nodes of 8 GPUs (API: num_gpus 'must be multiple of 8'), so gpu_min_count 8 (a 1-GPU workload pays for 8). Host CPU/RAM come with the node (vcpu_h/ram_gib_h 0); node CPU/RAM spec not published on the pricing page. Billing: 'Hourly billing: Pay per hour of cluster runtime' (docs); rounding of partial hours not stated.

modes.label: H100 HGX/SXM, spot (×8 node)
modes.note: Preemptible (public preview, Kubernetes only). Cannot be bought alone: every cluster needs at least one standard (on-demand or reserved) 8-GPU node, so the cheapest real spot setup is 8 standard GPUs + N x 8 preemptible GPUs; this per-GPU rate understates the true cost unless the workload already needs a standard node. Flat discount vs on-demand (not a bid), metered every 1-2 minutes, drain window of at most 5 minutes, no minimum-lifetime guarantee. Source: https://docs.together.ai/docs/preemptible-compute

plans.name: Self-serve (GPU clusters, on-demand)
plans.note: GPU Clusters on-demand is "fully self-serve": "None - pay hourly, terminate anytime", up to 256 GPUs, capacity "based on real-time availability" (https://www.together.ai/gpu-clusters, 2026-09-28). No platform fee published.

caveats: GPU cluster rates not valid for Code Sandbox. H100 dedicated inference $3.99 is a promotion ending 2026-09-30; $5.49 normal list. Cluster reservation windows are not serverless usage rates.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

On-demand (H100/H200/B200/B300) and spot cluster modes are priced per GPU with gpu_min_count 8; reserved modes are priced as always-on commit modes; dedicated-inference modes are unpriced. The gpu-clusters page lists H200/B200 cluster scale as '256 to 1,000 GPUs', so gpu_min_count 8 may understate the real minimum for those.

Reserved clusters: prepaid upfront, non-refundable, cannot be paused, auto-decommissioned at the end of the term (24 h email); usage beyond the reservation is billed at on-demand rates. Docs say reservations are 1-90 days while the pricing page sells 7-30 / 31-90 / 91-180 days and 181+ via sales, and the marketing page says 'Up to 6 months'.
The clusters API also accepts RTX_6000_PCI, L40_PCIE and H100_SXM_INF, and GB200/GB300 NVL72 are 'Contact us'; none has a published cluster price, so they are not listed in gpu_types.

fleet.tiers: On-demand self-serve up to 256 GPUs per cluster (H100 '8 to 256 GPUs'; H200/B200 listed '256 to 1,000'), capacity based on real-time availability; reserved self-serve 'Up to 4,000+ GPUs'; 181+ day reservations, GB200/GB300 NVL72 and B300 reserved via sales. The 64-GPU figure came from the March 2025 preview.
fleet.notes: Per-cluster supported size is not account-wide fresh GPU quota. Current pricing distinguishes on-demand and reserved products; account approval, payment checks and scale-review time not established.

snapshot_auto.quote: Local NVMe disks and node-local storage are ephemeral.
snapshot_auto.note: GPU Clusters (Kubernetes / Slurm-on-Kubernetes): no state capture on stop; node disks are ephemeral and only shared volumes persist. Reserved clusters cannot be paused and are decommissioned at term end.

volume_attach.quote: You can dynamically create and attach volumes to your cluster at cluster creation time, and resize as your data grows.
volume_attach.note: Shared volumes sized in whole TiB, resizable, persist beyond cluster deletion and can be reattached to other clusters. Attach at cluster creation (new or existing volume_id).

volume_shared.quote: Shared volumes are remote-attached, high-speed filesystems. They are created during cluster setup (or attached from an existing volume) and are accessible from all nodes.
volume_shared.note: Read-write; Kubernetes PV with ReadWriteMany (multiple pods across nodes), Slurm mounts it at /home on all compute and login nodes.

isolation.quote: Our Kubernetes runtime exposes all GPU devices to all containers on the host
isolation.note: GPU Clusters are Kubernetes (or Slurm-on-Kubernetes) clusters of dedicated bare-metal nodes; the customer-facing workload unit is a container/pod on those nodes, matching the card's existing top-level isolation value.

image_oci.note: Any container image can be run as a pod on the cluster.

docker_inside.quote: Use kubectl to interact with Kubernetes clusters for containerized workloads.
docker_inside.note: Workloads are containers/pods on Kubernetes; Slurm compute/login nodes also give sudo-level SSH access to the underlying Linux host where container tooling could be installed.

snapshot.note: No filesystem or memory snapshot/checkpoint capability for a whole node is documented; only PVC-backed shared volumes persist data.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Local NVMe disks and node-local storage are ephemeral.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI snapshot or checkpoint action for a cluster/node is documented.

fork.note: No cluster/node cloning feature is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Can I pause a cluster to save costs? Reserved clusters cannot be paused. You're charged for the full reservation period. On-demand clusters can be terminated and recreated later, but there's no pause function.
pause_resume.note: Explicitly no pause function for either billing type; the involuntary pause on credit exhaustion is not a user-controlled feature.

wake_on_request.quote: On-demand clusters: Run until manually terminated. Can be stopped/started anytime. No automatic decommissioning.
wake_on_request.note: No automatic wake-on-request mechanism is documented; clusters must be started/stopped manually.

persistent_disk.quote: Shared volumes (PVC): Persistent. Survives pod restarts, node reboots/migrations/recreations, cluster operations, and even cluster deletion.
persistent_disk.note: Shared volumes persist; local NVMe/node disk is explicitly ephemeral.

auto_stop_idle.quote: On-demand clusters: Run until manually terminated. Can be stopped/started anytime. No automatic decommissioning.
auto_stop_idle.note: No idle-based auto-stop is documented; only credit exhaustion or reservation end triggers stop/decommission.

live_resize.quote: auto_scale_max_gpus: Maximum number of GPUs to which the cluster can be auto-scaled up.
live_resize.note: Only cluster-level GPU node-count auto-scaling exists; no documented ability to change a single running node's CPU/RAM without recreating it.

client = Together()
response = client.beta.clusters.create(...)
lang_python.note: Together Python SDK manages clusters; Linux cluster nodes run arbitrary Python.

lang_node.note: Together TypeScript/JavaScript SDK manages clusters; Linux cluster nodes run arbitrary Node.js.

egress_http_rules.quote: Together AI does not charge for data transfer into or out of your cluster
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented for GPU cluster nodes.

guest_firewall.quote: sudo scontrol update NodeName=<node_name> State=drain Reason="<reason_for_draining>"
guest_firewall.note: derived: sudo/root-level SSH access to bare-metal Slurm/Kubernetes worker nodes implies nftables/iptables would work inside.

secret_proxy.quote: Full API access: Manage clusters via REST API or CLI.
secret_proxy.note: No first-party credential-injection proxy for outbound HTTP calls is documented; credentials are supplied by the user inside the cluster (env vars, files, Kubernetes secrets).

windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; only Linux nodes with NVIDIA drivers/CUDA are offered (card os: linux).

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; NVIDIA GPU HGX Linux nodes only.

arm64.quote: gpu_type: H100_SXM, H200_SXM, RTX_6000_PCI, L40_PCIE, B200_SXM, H100_SXM_INF, B300_SXM
arm64.note: All published GPU cluster node types are NVIDIA HGX/PCIe x86 servers; no ARM host option is documented.

self_host.quote: Self-serve AI-ready GPU clusters at scale.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; GPU Clusters is a managed service on Together's own datacenter capacity, not software you self-host.

byoc.quote: Deploy in any environment, with full control: Deploy on Together Cloud, your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), or on-premise.
byoc.note: The Together Enterprise Platform (inference/fine-tuning) supports VPC/on-prem deployment, but GPU Clusters (this card's product) is sold as Together's own bare-metal capacity, not deployed into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: Managed NVIDIA GPU cluster infrastructure for distributed training, fine-tuning, and large-scale inference.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the GPU Clusters orchestration platform itself is not published under an OSI license (Together does open-source some research code/models, but not this product).

hipaa.quote: Compliance with major industry standards such as SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA
hipaa.note: Stated at the Together Enterprise Platform / company level, not specific to GPU Clusters.

sso.quote: Single Sign-On enables your company to authenticate to your Together Organization through your company's existing Identity Provider (IdP) ... Together supports SSO via SAML and OIDC protocols
sso.note: Available for Scale and Enterprise accounts.

eu_data_residency.quote: Together supports private networking and VPC-based deployments, including in EU regions.
eu_data_residency.note: Card's existing regions list already includes 'eu'.

max_session_h.quote: On-demand clusters: Run until manually terminated. Can be stopped/started anytime. No automatic decommissioning.
max_session_h.note: Reserved clusters instead have a fixed prepaid term (1-90+ days) after which they are auto-decommissioned, but on-demand clusters (the base mode) have no session time limit.

nested_virt.quote: Bare-metal performance, InfiniBand networking, and managed orchestration — with flexible pricing for both on-demand and reserved capacity.
nested_virt.note: derived: nodes are dedicated bare-metal HGX servers, and docs give sudo-level SSH access to Kubernetes worker nodes and Slurm compute nodes ('sudo scontrol update NodeName=...'), so /dev/kvm should be usable inside; not explicitly documented as a feature.

public_ipv4.quote: public_ipv4: type: string description: Public IPv4 address of the GPU worker node.
public_ipv4.note: The cluster API schema returns a public_ipv4 field for both the control-plane node and each GPU worker node (GPUClusterGPUWorkerNode / GPUClusterControlPlaneNode objects).

inbound_https.quote: install_traefik: type: boolean default: false description: Whether to install Traefik ingress controller in the cluster. This field is only applicable for Kubernetes clusters and is false by default.
inbound_https.note: Kubernetes clusters can be created with load_balancer set to TRAEFIK, NGINX, or ISTIO (InstanceClusterConfig.load_balancer enum), which are HTTP(S) ingress controllers for routing external traffic to pods/services; disabled (NONE) by default so it is opt-in, not automatic.

ingress_rules.quote: Key-based commands use a proxy jump host: ssh -J <LOGIN>@ssh.<CLUSTER_ID>.<REGION>.cloud.together.ai <LOGIN>@<NODE_HOSTNAME>
ingress_rules.note: Node access is mediated through a per-cluster SSH jump host requiring OIDC sign-in or an uploaded SSH key (jumphost_enabled/ssh_ca_enabled in clusters-create.md), plus project-based admin/editor roles gating who can reach cluster resources at all; Kubernetes clusters can also add Traefik/Nginx/Istio as an ingress layer in front of exposed HTTP(S) ports.

egress_allowlist.quote: Together AI does not charge for data transfer into or out of your cluster, so you can move datasets, checkpoints, and results freely.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress rule feature is documented anywhere in the cluster management, API, or billing docs; free unrestricted data transfer is described instead.

static_egress_ip.quote: public_ipv4: type: string description: Public IPv4 address of the GPU worker node.
static_egress_ip.note: derived: each bare-metal node holds its own dedicated public_ipv4 (not a shared NAT gateway pool), so outbound traffic from that node uses the same stable address for the node's lifetime; not explicitly documented as a persistent/guaranteed egress IP feature, and node recreation could change it.

usage_api.quote: Returns an organization's billing usage for a month as cost-annotated line items grouped into time windows. Resource identifiers for attribution, varying by product. Product_name and cost in USD returned for each line item.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; GET /billing/usage REST API is documented and returns billing usage with cost-annotated line items that include resource attributes. API is in beta, requires per-org enablement. Documentation explicitly shows attributes vary by product (e.g., api_key_id, project_id for inference); GPU cluster breakdown by cluster_id inferred but not explicitly documented in API examples.
